title: Contents Packout & Storage — Calculation of the Customer-Billed Vault Storage Line
content:
**Calculation clause.** The line is charged while its period runs, and the period being billed is the storage period, counted in whole periods of the tier's period length from the custody start date, that contains the day the line is charged. The standard vault storage line for such a period is the vault count recorded on the job times the tier's vault rate for the full period, rounded to the cent, half up.

This Contents Packout & Storage clause prices the vault storage line billed to the customer on a Partial Contents Packout or Full Contents Packout job.

For a vault storage line priced under this clause, and only for such a line, the amount is figured as stated here; every other vault storage line is still billed in full on its period's first day at the vault rate times the vault count in force that day, rounded to the cent, half up.

## Quantities and where they come from

| Quantity | Source |
|---|---|
| The period being billed | the storage period, counted in whole periods of the tier's period length from the custody start date recorded on the job, that contains the day the line is charged |
| The vault count recorded on the job | the job record: the vaults filled at custody start, as later changed by vaults added or consolidated |
| The tier's vault rate and period length | the product's vault storage rate card for the job's tier |

## How the amounts combine

The amounts are combined in one order: the rate per vault is the tier's vault rate with any percentage applied first, then any factor multiplying that result, then any add per vault; that rate per vault is multiplied by the number of vaults; any amount figured per item is added to that product; the resulting sum is multiplied by the fraction of the period, and that figure is rounded once to the cent, half up, as the line amount.

Rounding is done once, on the final figure. Half up is applied with a tolerance of one billionth of a dollar (1e-09) added before rounding, so that a figure lying on a half cent always rounds up.

## Which period is being billed (hypothetical dates)

With a 30-day period length and custody starting on 1 March, the first period runs 1 March to 30 March, the second 31 March to 29 April, and the third from 30 April. A line charged on 12 April bills the second period, the one that contains 12 April.

## Worked figure (hypothetical inputs)

A job records 3 vaults, and the vault rate is taken as 100.00 for the illustration (not a tier figure). Three vaults times 100.00 for the full period is 300.00, and the line is 300.00. Had the rate been 99.995, the figure 299.985 would round half up to 299.99.
